rewrites.title: Chromatin-state mapping after signal removal
rewrites.description: Use ATAC-seq, CUT&RUN/ChIP for FOS/JUN, H3K27ac, and BAF remodeler marks, plus footprinting, in primed, rested, and naive cells to test whether AP-1-bound enhancers remain open after the signal is gone. Persistent accessibility at AP-1 motifs that correlates with enhanced re-induction would identify the chromatin carrier of memory.

rewrites.title: Lineage-tracked inheritance of memory through division
rewrites.description: Combine live imaging of an AP-1 reporter and a target-gene reporter with lineage tracking across several divisions after a transient stimulus. Compute mother-daughter and sister-cell correlations and the decay half-life, to test whether the memory state is mitotically heritable and clonal rather than a transient signaling effect.

rewrites.title: Single-molecule imaging of AP-1 residence across mitosis
rewrites.description: Track endogenously tagged Fos/Jun with live single-molecule imaging, and perform CUT&Tag/ChIP on sorted mitotic and post-mitotic cells, to measure whether AP-1 stays bound to mitotic chromosomes (bookmarking) and re-engages the same sites after division. Pair this with a reporter at a primed gene to test whether bookmarking predicts which daughter cells retain memory.

rewrites.title: Acute AP-1 degradation after priming
rewrites.description: Prime cells, let the stimulus decay, then rapidly deplete AP-1 (dTAG/AID degron of JUN/FOS, or dominant-negative A-FOS). Measure chromatin accessibility and transcription at one later time point versus controls. Loss of the primed state means AP-1 is needed to maintain memory; persistence means AP-1 only initiates it.

rewrites.title: Model-guided AP-1 depletion at different times after priming
rewrites.description: Build a dynamical model with positive feedback (FOS/JUN autoinduction and chromatin) fit to ramp and relaxation data, and use it to predict thresholds. Test it by acutely degrading AP-1 (degron, CRISPRi) at different times after priming: if AP-1 carries the memory, loss after priming should erase the primed response; if chromatin carries it, the response should persist and could be restored when AP-1 is returned.

rewrites.title: Optogenetic or degron pulse-chase of AP-1 timing
rewrites.description: Use an optogenetically controlled or auxin-degron c-Jun/Fos to deliver defined activity pulses and to remove AP-1 at set times after priming (not only during it). If memory persists after degradation, AP-1 only initiates it; if memory decays when AP-1 is removed, AP-1 maintains it.

rewrites.title: Motif-mutated enhancers with epigenetic readout
rewrites.description: Use CRISPR base editing to mutate single AP-1 sites at memory-associated enhancers. Then test whether primed accessibility, nearby H3K27ac, and faster re-induction of the target gene are lost. This tests whether the sites themselves are needed at specific loci, in contrast to global AP-1 loss.

rewrites.title: AP-1 bookmarking across cell divisions in patient-derived cells
rewrites.description: In patient-derived primary cells or organoids, use CUT&RUN/ChIP-seq on mitotically enriched versus interphase cells, and live imaging of endogenously tagged FOS/JUN alleles, to determine whether AP-1 stays on chromatin through division. Combine this with lineage-tracing barcodes or clonal expansion to test whether daughter cells inherit the AP-1 state, a requirement for cellular memory.

rewrites.title: AP-1 protein turnover versus persistence of memory
rewrites.description: Use SNAP- or HaloTag-labelled FOS/JUN with pulse-chase labelling to measure AP-1 protein and DNA-bound half-lives in the same cells where memory persists. Also mutate AP-1 motifs at memory-associated enhancers (base editing) and measure 3D contacts by Micro-C or Hi-C. If memory lasts well beyond AP-1 turnover, this would point toward an epigenetic or 3D-architecture-based mechanism rather than a self-sustaining AP-1 feedback loop.

rewrites.title: Erase, rewrite, and repeated cycling with targeted perturbations
rewrites.description: Erase the stored state with AP-1-directed interventions (auxin degron on FOS/JUN, dominant-negative A-FOS, or dCas9-KRAB/HDAC recruitment to specific AP-1 enhancers), re-apply the stimulus to test rewriting, and repeat write/erase cycles to detect degradation or drift. Clean erasure by an AP-1-specific perturbation with intact rewriting would indicate AP-1 is the causal storage element rather than a correlate of another persistent change.

rewrites.title: Motif-level editing at primed AP-1 sites
rewrites.description: Use targeted editing or CRISPRi tiling to disrupt individual AP-1 motifs within primed enhancers without altering the factor itself, then measure the response to a second stimulus. This distinguishes site-specific memory elements from a global AP-1 dosage effect.

rewrites.title: Single-molecule nucleosome footprinting at memory loci
rewrites.description: Use Fiber-seq or SMF/NOMe-seq on primed versus naive cells to read nucleosome positions and TF occupancy on single DNA molecules at AP-1 sites after washout. This shows whether memory is a stable open state in a subpopulation of alleles (bimodal, heritable) or a graded shift, and whether AP-1 is still bound or has been replaced by a remodeled nucleosome pattern.

rewrites.title: Cross-tissue and human comparison of AP-1-dependent memory
rewrites.description: Compare AP-1 occupancy (CUT&RUN), accessibility and responses across tissues with documented memory, such as post-inflammation epithelial stem cells, trained-immunity monocytes and injured neurons, in mice with conditional AP-1 knockouts. Add human cells from people with prior exposure (e.g., BCG vaccination, past inflammatory episodes) to test whether AP-1-dependent memory is general and to define its duration and reversibility.

rewrites.title: Enhancer occupancy persistence after stimulus washout
rewrites.description: Knock in endogenous HaloTag or degron-tagged FOS and JUN, and track single-cell AP-1 occupancy and enhancer accessibility by live imaging and CUT&Tag for days after a transient stimulus is removed. Memory requires that occupancy or chromatin state outlast both the signal and the transcriptional output, so a decoupling of these timescales would be the key result.

rewrites.title: Decay per unit time versus per cell division
rewrites.description: Compare decay of the stimulus-induced state in cell-cycle-arrested versus cycling cells (CDK4/6 inhibition, serum starvation, contact inhibition) over matched elapsed time, and use EdU- or sister-chromatid-resolved readouts to test whether loss occurs specifically at replication. Template-copied chromatin memory should decay per division, whereas protein-level or metabolic memory should decay with time.

rewrites.title: Hysteresis and bistability test with a feedback model
rewrites.description: Expose cells to increasing and then decreasing stimulus doses and measure single-cell AP-1 activity and target output, looking for bimodal distributions and path-dependent thresholds. Fit a model of c-Jun autoregulation, and test its predictions by breaking the feedback loop, for example by mutating the AP-1 site in the JUN promoter.

rewrites.title: AP-1 site editing and synthetic recruitment
rewrites.description: Use CRISPR to mutate or insert AP-1 motifs at candidate enhancers, or to recruit dCas9 AP-1 activators or repressors. Then test whether the primed response, accessibility and re-induction speed change at those loci. This gives causal evidence at specific sites and tests whether AP-1 sites are sufficient to create memory at naive loci. Also perturb partners such as pioneer factors or SWI/SNF to identify other requirements.

rewrites.title: Degron separation of establishment versus maintenance
rewrites.description: Knock dTAG or auxin-inducible degrons into endogenous FOSL1/JUN (or express a dominant-negative A-FOS under a Tet promoter) so AP-1 can be removed either during a priming stimulus or only after the primed state is established, then compare ATAC-seq and RNA-seq outcomes. If late depletion collapses the primed state, AP-1 is the memory carrier; if it leaves the state intact, AP-1 only establishes a state stored elsewhere, e.g., in chromatin or DNA methylation.

rewrites.title: Reporter panel varying AP-1 site architecture
rewrites.description: Integrate at a fixed safe-harbor locus a panel of reporters whose enhancers differ in AP-1 site number, affinity, spacing and neighboring cofactor motifs, then run identical prime–wait–rechallenge protocols on each. This identifies the minimal cis architecture sufficient to store a transient AP-1 input and shows which features set memory duration.

rewrites.title: Division-coupled inheritance of memory in sorted daughter cells
rewrites.description: Track HaloTag-labeled JUN or FOS with live imaging through one or more cell divisions after a priming stimulus, then sort daughter cells by nuclear AP-1 level and challenge them with re-stimulation. This tests whether memory is inherited through mitosis via bookmarking or re-established de novo by each daughter.
